qs.q: A 4-year-old child develops edema and hematuria 2 weeks after a skin impetigo infection. Urinalysis shows red cell casts. Which immunological mechanism is primarily responsible for this glomerulonephritis?
o: Type II hypersensitivity targeting glomerular basement membrane
Autoantibody production directed against streptococcal M protein
Type IV delayed hypersensitivity mediated by T-cell injury
Direct bacterial invasion occurring within glomerular capillaries
Type III hypersensitivity characterized by immune complex deposition
qs.e: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is a Type III hypersensitivity reaction involving immune complex deposition in the glomeruli.

qs.q: An 8-year-old girl develops gross hematuria, periorbital edema, and hypertension two weeks after recovering from impetigo. Renal biopsy demonstrates subepithelial immune complex humps. This nephritic syndrome is primarily initiated by:
qs.e: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is caused by the deposition of circulating immune complexes in the glomerular basement membrane.
